title: Scooter & Bike Track
strapline: Round the track, mind the crossing, wait at the red light — big movement and real road sense on wheels.
intent: Children build gross-motor power, balance and coordination — pedalling, scooting, steering, braking and stopping.
Children learn to judge speed and space, negotiating a shared track without crashing.
Children practise real road sense in miniature — stopping at the crossing, waiting at the light, looking before they go.
Children cooperate on a busy track: taking turns on favourite bikes, giving way, queuing at the petrol station.
Children experience the sheer joy and confidence of moving fast under their own power.
implementation: Chalk or tape a track with a clear direction of travel, a crossing and a couple of junctions.
Offer a graduated fleet — sit-and-ride, balance bikes, trikes, scooters — so every child finds their edge.
Add a working traffic light or a stop/go lollipop and model stopping, looking and waiting.
Coach the body talk quietly — 'push, push, glide', 'squeeze to stop', 'look before you turn' — then let them ride.
Set up a petrol station, a car wash and a repair bay so wheels have destinations and jobs.
Manage the sharing of popular bikes openly — a sand-timer turn, a waiting list on a clipboard.
Talk about being out of breath, hot and needing a drink after a fast lap.
key_questions: How do you make your scooter stop safely?
What do you do when the light turns red?
There's someone on the crossing — what should you do?
How does your body feel after that fast lap round the track?
Whose turn is next on the big trike — how will we know?

impact.text: Children pedal, scoot, steer, brake and negotiate the track with growing control and confidence.
Children judge speed and space, avoiding crashes and giving way on a shared track.
Children stop at the crossing, wait at the light and look before they go, showing early road sense.
Children take turns on favourite wheels and wait — sometimes gracefully — for their go.
Children notice their bodies after exertion — hot, thirsty, out of breath — and do something about it.
Younger children push, scoot and balance on low ride-ons, building the strength for pedalling.

enhancements: A taped or chalked track with arrows, a crossing and junctions.
A traffic light or stop/go lollipop for a child to operate.
A petrol station with a hose (rope), a till and pretend money.
A repair bay with tyre pumps, spanners and a mechanic's clipboard.
Numbered parking bays and a bike wash with sponges and buckets.
Hi-vis waistcoats, helmets and 'L' plates for new riders.
A start/finish line and a sand-timer for fair-turn races.

playing_exploring: Children throw themselves into fast, physical play and test what their bodies can do.
They explore the track's rules by riding them — what happens if I don't stop?
active_learning: Children practise a wobble into a glide, lap after lap, until it clicks.
Keeping the busy track flowing takes real concentration and give-and-take.
creating_thinking: Children invent routes, races and rules for the crossing.
They solve the traffic jam and the shared-bike problem with their own systems.
